title: Mackinnon:
headline: The surprise is not that people give. It is how rarely they get the chance.
story: Mackinnon, to camera, one question: what still surprises you? Not the generosity. People want to help. What surprises her is how often they are not given the chance.

Then the proof: donors who stay for ten years, and Andrew and Danya, who still give every month after marriage, moves and kids. The donor is the one who feels grateful. Warm and human. It ends on “the hunger we all have for it.”
do: Open on frame 1 with the question as top text.
Keep her natural pauses between the short lines.
Name super large, first name only, after the question leaves.
Cut before the thumbs-up at the end of the clip.
dont: No title card or logo at 0:00.
No B-roll from the old hospital-entrance sequence.
No more than one brand element on screen at a time.
No slow motion or dramatic push-ins.

bp_intro: All source times are in Mincho5162.MP4 (1:15, one 4K camera, Mackinnon only, one clean take). Times come from the transcript.json and are accurate to about 0.2 s. Find exact in and out points on the waveform. Every frame is from the real file. The yellow box shows the 9:16 crop.

rows.frame_alt: Mackinnon in a beige blouse, dark green wall and curtain behind, mid-sentence
rows.visual: Mackinnon, wide and locked-off. In-point on “The thing”. She already looks at the lens.
rows.motion: Question on top from frame 1, top third: What still surprises you? Lato Bold, Watsi yellow #FFCC33, soft shadow. Cut on. Stays to 00:05.5. Captions start with her voice.

voice.quote: The thing that surprises me most about this work isn't actually the generosity.

rows.music: Music enters under her first word. Warm, sustained piano or guitar bed, 18–20 dB under her voice. No drums.

rows.visual: Same shot. Keep each small pause between the three short lines.
rows.motion: Question fades out at 00:05.5 (6 frames). Name super “Mackinnon” right after it, 00:06–00:08, lower left, above the captions, large. First name only.

voice.quote: People want to help. They always have. That's not the surprise.

rows.frame_alt: Mackinnon, hands together, looking at the lens
rows.visual: 106% punch-in on “What surprises me”. This is the idea of the video.

voice.quote: What surprises me is how often people simply aren't given the chance.

rows.visual: Back to 100%. Hard cut. Stay on her. If it drags, one 104% punch-in on “People are waiting”.
rows.motion: Captions only. Write the years as numbers: “9, 10, 11 years”.

voice.quote: We have donors who've been giving every month for 9, 10, 11 years, not because we push them, but because they found something that felt real and they don't want to stop. People are waiting for something they can actually trust, a way to give that shows them the person, shares the outcome, and doesn't disappear into a logo and a distant promise.

rows.visual: On her. She smiles here. Let it play.
rows.motion: Captions only. Spell it Danya. The transcript says “Dania”: that is wrong.

voice.quote: I think of Andrew and Danya, giving every month since 2014. They've gotten married, changed jobs, moved across the country, had kids, and they still give every month for more than a decade. Danya said she gets hit with a wave of gratitude whenever an update email comes in. She's the one who's grateful.

rows.music: Small lift on “wave of gratitude”. Not a swell.

rows.motion: Captions only. The transcript writes “Thanks for WOTC”. Her script says “Thanks to Watsi”. Caption what she really says. Check by ear.

voice.quote: I spend a lot of my time thanking donors, and often their response is, no, thank you. Thanks for Watsi for making this possible, and that still gets me.

rows.visual: On her. Hold 0.7 s after “for it”, then cut to the end card. Cut before the end of the clip (visual.json shows a thumbs-up after the take).

voice.quote: When you give people something real, they hold on. That's what keeps surprising me, not the generosity, but the hunger we all have for it.

rows.visual: Clean end card. Light cyan #D3EDFA background. Navy is never a background.
rows.motion: watsi.org, all lowercase, Lato, navy #2E2844. One line. Nothing under it. No stats, no donate button.

Uppbeat, like other Watsi cuts. Save the license certificate with the project: YouTube flagged an Uppbeat track on a Watsi upload on 7 Oct.
tech: 3840×2160, 23.976 fps, 2-ch audio recorded into the camera (same camera and room as Mincho5163)
1080×1920 at 23.976 fps. Same as the source. No frame-rate change.
A 9:16 crop of 4K is 1215×2160, so it is sharper than 1080×1920. Punch-ins up to 112% stay native. The room is dim: lift exposure and skin a little, keep it natural.
2 channels recorded into the camera. Pick the live channel on the waveform and map it to both sides. Mute the other. (Not measured: the Drive download limit stopped the audio check.)
Lato Bold, white, soft shadow, large. Pop word by word. No highlight box, no shading block. One line at a time. Always on screen, also in pauses. Keep the bottom 20% clear for app buttons.
checklist: Read every caption against the audio. Sonam checks every word, and typos are her top complaint.
The transcript writes “WOTC”. It is Watsi, capital W only. The URL is watsi.org, all lowercase.
The question is on screen from frame 1 and stays at least 5 seconds.
Name super “Mackinnon” is large, first name only, and never at 0:00.
Captions never drop out, even in pauses.
Keep her natural pauses. The delivery must sound like her, not a teleprompter.
Danya is spelled with a y. Andrew and Danya, “since 2014”.
End card: watsi.org, lowercase, nothing under it.

decisions.b: Nick's brief calls this a direct fit for the Who Gives campaign. If it posts as Who Gives, the rules change: no music and the “Tell us your story” close. If not, it ships as planned here. Nick decides before V1.

client_note: Why this matters: Watsi's best content has one real person at the center. Here the people are Andrew and Danya, through Mackinnon. Let their story carry it.
